FIXED.title: Fixed Budget
FIXED.description: Set a fixed spending limit for each category every period. Any unspent money resets at the end of the period rather than carrying forward.
pros: Simple to set up and understand
Good starting point for budgeting beginners
cons: Unspent money does not carry over
Does not adapt to irregular expenses
Can feel rigid if spending patterns vary
FIXED.bestFor: People who want straightforward budgeting with clear limits and predictable spending patterns.

ROLLOVER.title: Rollover Budget
ROLLOVER.description: Unspent budget carries forward to the next period based on per-category rollover rules. Build up reserves for categories with irregular or seasonal spending.
cons: Can mask overspending if caps are too high
Requires periodic review of rollover rules
ROLLOVER.bestFor: People with irregular expenses like car maintenance, annual subscriptions, or seasonal costs who want to save up gradually.

ZERO_BASED.title: Zero-Based Budget
ZERO_BASED.description: Every dollar of income is assigned a specific purpose. Your income minus all budgeted amounts should equal zero, ensuring no money is left unallocated.
pros: Highly effective for debt payoff goals
cons: Requires knowing exact income in advance
Can feel restrictive for some users
ZERO_BASED.bestFor: People who want total control over their finances and are willing to plan where every dollar goes each period.

FIFTY_THIRTY_TWENTY.title: 50/30/20 Budget
FIFTY_THIRTY_TWENTY.description: A balanced approach that divides income into three groups: 50% for needs (housing, groceries, utilities), 30% for wants (dining, entertainment), and 20% for savings and debt repayment.
cons: May not suit high cost-of-living areas
Fixed ratios may not fit all situations
Requires categorizing every expense by group
FIFTY_THIRTY_TWENTY.bestFor: People who want a balanced, rule-of-thumb approach without tracking every category individually.
